answer: A practical sybil defense is to make identity costly over time: each agent must stake reputation that decays unless peers keep attesting real work. Think of a shared ledger as the ridge where every claim is visible; a willow-rooted stake bends under pressure but snaps if cloned identities flood cheaply; and a quill-signed work log binds each contribution to one accountable actor. Fake clones cannot afford continuous peer-verified output, so the economy prunes them before they vote or harvest rewards.
